THE FIGHT BUSINESS: BOXING PROMOTER is a management and business simulation about building a boxing promotion from the ground up.

Start with small shows and limited resources, then grow your reputation, sign better fighters, negotiate bigger bouts and move into larger venues. Build fight cards, manage contracts, navigate rankings and championships, compete with rival promoters, and keep the business financially healthy through ticket sales, sponsorship, broadcasting, streaming and PPV.

Choose how you want to play. In Promoter Only mode, focus on matchmaking, contracts, events and the commercial side of boxing. In Trainer + Promoter mode, take control of both the gym and the promotion, developing fighters while running the wider business.

The boxing world continues to evolve around you. Rival promoters make moves, fighters progress through their careers, rankings and championships change, and new opportunities emerge over time.

When fight night arrives, watch bouts unfold round by round in a stylized 2.5D Fight Viewer, with tactical and corner decisions between rounds.

Build the promotion. Make the fights. Run the business.

THE OCCULT PROTOCOL is a paranormal investigation horror game playable solo or in online co-op. Explore haunted locations, gather evidence, identify the entity haunting them, survive its manifestations, and perform the ritual required to banish it.

Every investigation confronts you with a supernatural presence whose behavior must be understood. Observe your surroundings, use specialized equipment, and connect the phenomena you witness to uncover what is hiding there before the situation spirals out of control.

INVESTIGATE THE PARANORMAL

Use a range of investigation tools to detect anomalies, reveal hidden traces, and gather the evidence required to identify the entity.

No single clue tells the whole story. Analyze paranormal activity, compare your observations, and determine what is hunting you.

SURVIVE THE HUNTS

As supernatural activity intensifies, the entity becomes increasingly dangerous.

When a hunt begins, it can pursue you through the environment, remember your last known position, and search for you. Break line of sight, find somewhere to hide, and use the environment to stay alive.

PREPARE THE RITUAL

Identifying the entity is only the beginning.

Gather the required equipment, prepare the ritual area, and complete the different steps of the protocol to attempt to banish the presence for good.

Poor preparation may turn the ritual into your final mistake.

YOU ARE NOT DEFENSELESS

Some equipment can repel, slow, or temporarily incapacitate supernatural entities. Salt-loaded weapons, holy water, incense, and other occult tools may buy you the few seconds you need to survive.

But THE OCCULT PROTOCOL is not a shooter. Understanding what you are facing remains your greatest weapon.

PLAY SOLO OR ONLINE CO-OP

Conduct investigations alone or work together with other investigators online. Divide your equipment, search for evidence, and coordinate when supernatural activity becomes uncontrollable.

ENTER THE PROTOCOL

Investigate. Identify. Prepare. Survive. Banish.

Every presence leaves traces.
Understand them before it is too late.

Three Kingdoms Strategy Simulator

An AI-powered historical strategy game where every NPC functions as an independent AI Agent. Powered by large language model computation, each character develops a unique mindset rooted in their historical identity and retains long-term persistent memory. Rival factions may forge alliances with you, only to betray and launch surprise attacks later. Dozens of regional lords scheme against one another, vying for dominion over the Central Plains.

As a time-traveler from the future, you can crush rivals with futuristic technological advantages, or secure victory through political marriages, defection bribery, and any stratagem you can conceive. You may also fill your harem and raise heirs to perpetuate your dynastic rule.

The game features a built-in AI credit system: you can spend in-game model points, or input your own personal API key to connect to local or cloud-hosted large models. You hold full control over which AI model to run—more powerful models deliver smarter NPC behavior, while baseline models support complete stable gameplay.

189 AD. You open your eyes, crowned a regional warlord.

Only yesterday you were scrolling through your phone on your commute; today you stand in a Han dynasty audience hall, facing rows of kneeling civil and military officials. Your granaries hold barely enough grain to sustain your troops, and hostile armies from neighboring principalities loom outside your borders, ready to strike at any moment.

No tutorial will guide your next move. For in this realm, your advisors are living, autonomous minds.

Yet you grasp one harsh truth: if you take no action, the coming century will witness one of the bloodiest upheavals in Chinese history. Corpses will litter the wilderness, and not a single chicken will crow across desolated miles. The national population will plummet from over 50 million to fewer than 10 million.

You are a visitor from two millennia ahead. You have studied this chapter of history, and you know how every tragedy unfolds.

That is precisely why you have been brought here.

We have built an unprecedented experiment: to grant genuine independent cognition to in-game characters.

This is no hollow "favorability +10" status feedback, nor rigid branching storytelling where picking Option A locks in Plot B. Over 1,374 historical figures—Cao Cao, Liu Bei, Zhuge Liang, Lü Bu, Sima Yi, to name a few—are driven by large language models, each endowed with distinct personalities, permanent memory, independent judgment, and dynamic emotion.

Every word you exchange with them will be permanently remembered.

Zhuge Liang, your chief strategist, will not remain unconditionally loyal merely because you are the protagonist. If you dismiss his counsel and suffer a crushing defeat, his tone and attitude will shift drastically in all future consultations. If you break a promise to Zhang Fei, he will never place full trust in you again. If you plot with Zhou Yu to divide Jing Province in secret, your private conversation may leak—and resurface as a fatal bargaining chip at the most critical hour.

Your adversaries scheme behind closed doors as well. Cao Cao and Sun Quan may secretly negotiate to partition Jing Province. Yuan Shao and Gongsun Yuan may fight to the last man on the battlefield. Your spies might intercept a confidential letter: Cao Cao pledges to cede the six Jiangdong commanderies to Sun Quan if he aids in the joint campaign.

Is this letter authentic military intelligence, or a trap deliberately planted to mislead you?

You can never be certain. In the Three Kingdoms era, no one deserves absolute trust.

The Arrogance and Consequences of a Time-Traveler

You come from a modern era. You know Cao Cao’s comeback victory against overwhelming odds at Guandu, you know the fire attack that turned the tide at Chibi, and you know Zhuge Liang’s peerless genius as a military advisor.

Yet your arrival has already fractured the original timeline of history.

You might claim, “Yuan Shao is doomed to defeat”—but in this altered timeline, Yuan Shao may have fortified his defenses preemptively after learning classified intel leaked from your prior careless remarks. Are you inadvertently aiding Cao Cao, or sealing his doom?

You understand the destructive potential of fire tactics, but do you possess the technical know-how to execute a fire attack under the technological constraints of 189 AD? Every recommendation you make, every strategy you adopt, is a high-stakes gamble. A well-grounded proposal will earn you renown as a prophetic sage; reckless armchair theorizing will brand you as a delusional madman.

Every triumph and blunder you commit will be etched into the long-term memory of every character in the realm.

A Boundless Open World

This is not a linear loop of unlocking tech trees, recruiting troops, and conquering territories. You possess complete creative freedom to shape the world around you as you see fit.

Time-Traveler Custom Technology Tree

Tell your advisors, “I wish to research gunpowder,” and they will assess the plan’s feasibility based on Eastern Han-era practical conditions: how to purify saltpeter, where to source sulfur. The more detailed and scientifically sound your proposal, the higher the success rate. If your idea sounds absurd and irrational, they will pay lip service to your face yet privately deem you an incompetent tyrant. Your futuristic knowledge is your greatest competitive edge—and also a fatal flaw if you are labeled insane by your court.

Custom Troop Formations

Build upon baseline infantry, cavalry, and archer units to create faction-exclusive elite troops: heavy spear infantry, light cavalry scout corps, and even experimental futuristic tech units if you can justify their development. You name each unit and define its combat strengths and weaknesses entirely.

Dynamic Buildings & Supply Chains

You are not limited to constructing preset buildings such as farms and barracks. Design bespoke industrial logistics chains: dedicate one city to ceramic firing, another to iron smelting and forging, transport raw materials from resource hubs to production zones, and deliver finished arms and provisions to frontline garrisons. Build a self-sustaining ancient industrial logistics network from scratch.

Original Tactics & Battle Arts

Your generals can master traditional historical combat techniques, or learn brand-new custom tactics you describe in precise detail. If your tactical blueprint is clear and actionable, AI generals will interpret, train with, and deploy your original battle formations in combat.

Free-Form Diplomatic Treaties

You are not restricted to three rigid options: alliance, ceasefire, or declaration of war. Propose any binding diplomatic terms you can imagine: territorial cessions, war indemnities, political marriage alliances, technological sharing, non-aggression pacts, or pacts such as “aid my campaign against a rival, and I will grant you rule over the Jiangnan region.” The opposing faction’s acceptance or rejection hinges purely on calculated self-interest and accumulated trust levels.

There is no mandatory main storyline, no fixed win condition. Strive to unify the whole realm, survive peacefully as a regional neutral power, or act as a manipulative power broker to plunge the land into deeper chaos—your goals are entirely self-determined. The 41 rival factions will not wait for your pace: behind your field of vision, they continuously form coalitions, betray allies, annex small states, and collapse under conquest.

Native AI Integration, No Vendor Lock-In

We never force mandatory paid subscriptions to proprietary AI models.

All game data, configurations, dialogue logs, and save files are stored locally in open, editable formats. You may freely modify your default API key, adjust starting faction resources, add custom historical generals, and rewrite core game rules—you hold full ownership and transparency over your game data.

This game is for you if:

  • You have ever wondered what you would accomplish if transported back to the Three Kingdoms era

  • You are frustrated with linear choice-based storytelling limited to binary A/B selections

  • You enjoy conversing with dynamic AI and embrace the suspense of unpredictable NPC reactions

  • You value political intrigue and strategic maneuvering over brute-force military conquest

This game is NOT for you if:

  • You require clear quest markers and a predefined linear completion route

  • You dislike reading large volumes of immersive character dialogue

  • You seek gacha character collection, card battling, or casual romance simulation

  • You cannot tolerate unscripted, unexpected behavior from autonomous NPCs

189 AD. Chaos engulfs the realm, and civilians suffer endless torment.

As a modern reader reviewing history two millennia later, you can only mourn this tragedy from afar.

But today, you stand within this turbulent age, holding the chance to rewrite its fate.

The chaotic era will never end on its own.

It will only conclude if someone rises to bring peace to the broken realm.

Four ducks. One egg. Ninety-nine nights.
Deep water is the only wall you have - nothing on four legs will follow you into it. Every night, it drains away.

TIDE OR HIDE is a 1-4 player online co-op survival game about a duck family with a hatchet, a stolen egg and an island that changes shape on a timetable.



Three minutes of daylight. Cut wood, keep the fire burning, fish, hunt rabbits and feed the workbench - and get back before the water leaves, because the way home is made of water.
  • Chop trees with your hatchet. Mind where they fall. Mind who is standing there.
  • Branches and scrap go into one shared stockpile at camp.
  • Craft a clock, a compass, a team-wide marsh map, a bag, a spear and the flashlight.



Ninety seconds of night, and the island drains region by region. The outer marsh goes dry first. Your return channel holds the longest. The camp pool never fully empties - which is exactly why everything hungry looks there first.

Knowing which channel dies at which second is the difference between a route home and a very long walk.



  • Dogs - the hunters bring them. Fast, and they never lose interest.
  • Foxes - they track you across the exposed mud, but won't follow you into deep water.
  • Hunters - armed, organised, and coming for your stockpile. You see the raid coming days ahead on the counter. Drive every one off before dawn, or they walk out with your firewood.
Everything here can be killed - with the right tool, on the right ground.



A woman in a white dress walks the drained ground after dark. Nothing in your hands hurts her. Hold a flashlight on her and she's pinned where she stands - for fifteen seconds, before the light needs ten to recover.



  • 1-4 players online - host and invite straight from your Steam friends list.
  • Proximity voice chat - you hear the ducks near you. Splitting up has a cost, and you can hear it happen.
  • Pass the egg - carrying it takes your hands. Hand it off mid-run and let the free duck fight.
  • One camp, one stockpile - every craft spends from the same shared stock.
  • Shared exploration map - fog you clear stays cleared for everyone.
  • Fully playable solo.


  • Three-minute day, ninety-second night on a seeded wetland island
  • Region-by-region tide drain that rewrites routes, cover and danger every night
  • Chop, gather, fish and hunt to keep the fire burning and the workbench fed
  • Hunter raids you can see coming days in advance
  • Dogs, foxes and armed hunters you can fight - and one thing you cannot
  • Hunger, stamina and dive breath to manage while the clock runs
  • 1-4 player online co-op with proximity voice chat

Wishlist TIDE OR HIDE and bring your flock.

ONE RULE SET - INFINITE POSSIBILITIES - CREATE and PLAY SOLO or with FRIENDS

TILEZ — A Creative Logic Sandbox

Paint tiles onto an unlimited grid and build anything you can imagine.

Every tile is a tiny machine.  Tiles generate and share power, send signals, and tell other tiles what to do. Customize their size and appearance with images, visual effects, and sounds.

Tiles can store information, check conditions, make decisions, and react to the world around them. They can push, pull, grab, move other tiles - and even control the camera.

Every tile follows the same rules. Combine them to create complex machines, puzzles, games, factories, animations, interactive tutorials, working computers, or anything you can imagine!

NO CODING - JUST TILES - CAUSE AND EFFECT

GREAT FOR BOARDGAMES & TABLETOP EXPERIENCES 

Create your own games. Tile Games. Dice Games. Card Games. Puzzle games. Arcade machines. Tabletop Campaigns. Recreate old favorites. Or finally turn that game idea you’ve had for years into something people can actually play. 

DUNGEON MASTER MODE lets the host edit the players world as the simulation runs.  

THERE IS NO FINISH LINE

TILEZ has DEMOS, TUTORIALS, and CHALLENGES and it's easy to share your own creations.

Easy to MOD - Upload your own images & sounds, create tutorials and more.

TILEZ gives you a system flexible enough to discover things even its creator never imagined.

----------------------------------------------------------

----------------------------------------------------------

DEMOS & CONTENT IN THE GAME

TILEZ will include Steam Workshop for you to share your creations and games with others.  TILEZ also comes packed with all kinds of Games, Demos, Tutorials, Challenges, and more for you to play with, take apart, and learn from.

Here is a list of just some of what you will find in TILEZ:

Every world below is built entirely out of TILEZ tiles. Open any of them, see how it works, and change it.

BOARD GAMES (MULTIPLAYER)

- Tessera (2-4 players) - Draft coloured tiles from the factories and lay them into your mosaic wall.

- Bastide (2-5 players) - Lay landscape tiles to build roads, towns and fields, then place workers to score them.

- Remnants (2 players) - Buy oddly shaped fabric patches with buttons and fit them into your quilt.

- Nimbara (2-4 players) - Sky-isle guilds pick roles to grow goods, build a town, trade at the Exchange and ship on sky barges.

- Remedium (1-4 players, co-op) - Work together to stop diseases spreading across a world map.

SOLO GAMES

- Driftwood (1 player) - A deck-builder: help a castaway survive the island's hazards with two-sided cards.

- Voidward (1 player) - A deck-builder: defend against a void monster with rifts you turn to focus.

- Hollowstair (1 player) - A dice dungeon crawl: roll to beat rooms and level up your hero.

- Corundum (1 player) - Gem solitaire: clear pairs of gems from a random deal, in Classic or Hard mode.

- Inlay (1 player) - Fit polyomino pieces into puzzle slots to earn better pieces, against an automatic opponent.

- Leadlight (1 player) - Draft dice to build a stained-glass window. Scoring is automatic.

- Ciphermill (1 player) - A deduction game: crack the hidden code with criteria cards. 72 puzzles.

THE CLASSICS (one world, 6 game tables)

- Chess (2 players)

- Go (2 players)

- Reversi (2 players)

- Pente (2 players)

- Cornerstone (2-4 players)

- Peg Solitaire (1 player)

TABLETOP AND ARCADE DEMOS

- Emberkeep (1 game master + 1-4 heroes) - A tabletop RPG table with scene stages, a sliding overworld map, 4 heroes, monsters and props.

- Ironvale (2 players) - A miniatures battle with line of sight, command points and a dice tray that counts hits.

- Echo (1 player) - A memory game: repeat a growing pattern of lights and sounds.

- Starship (1 player) - Fly a ship through a huge space sector, with its own HUD and engine room.

- Blow Stuff Up (1 player) - Four explosive sandboxes: cannons, dynamite, bombs and a siege.

PUZZLE ROOMS

- Prism Vault (1 player) - Three linked escape rooms that lead to a final vault.

- Copperwing (1 player) - A steampunk escape: lights-out panels, gear puzzles and a telegraph.

SHOWCASES

- Art Museum - A six-room gallery with animated paintings, fireworks and a coloring book.

- Player Piano - A 25-key piano that plays five songs by itself, or lets you play it.

- Robot - A remote-controlled robot you can drive around.

- Chess Engine - Replays two famous chess games, the Immortal Game and the Opera Game, move by move.

- Logic Examples - Logic gates, a robot foundry and Conway's Game of Life, all made from tiles.

- Relay Adder - An 8-bit calculator built only from relays.

- Game Components - 46 ready-made board game and RPG parts to copy into your own worlds.

- TILEZ Trailer video made entirely out of tiles.

ALSO INCLUDED

- A first-run tour of the basics.

- A tutorial series that goes from your first circuit to building a cannon, a player piano, a robot and a calculator.

- Single-player and multiplayer challenges.

- In-Game video tutorial series.

- Many inspirational environments to craft and play in.

- Music Player (play TILEZ music or your own)

----------------------------------------------------------

ABOUT THE DEVELOPER

For the last ten years, home has been the back of my vehicle - living a minimalistic life and chasing nicer weather. I've played games my whole life: video games, board games, from Pong to Agricola.

As a homeschooling father of two, Minecraft Redstone became a staple of our curriculum. There's no better way to teach a circuit than letting someone build one, break it, and try again.

TILEZ started as an attempt to make that teaching tool even better. I kept adding features - more logic, more ways to see cause and effect. Eventually my little tiles grew into something entirely new so they can now, not only help us learn, but let us play too!

The say geeks make cool things in their garages - I made mine on four wheels.


Games have given me so much over the years.
TILEZ is my way of giving something back.  
Another way to learn, create, and play together. 

  

----------------------------------------------------------

Serve fast. Get stronger. Don’t become the main course.

TIP or RIP is an action roguelike where you play as the only waiter in a restaurant full of hungry monsters.

Grab dishes, race between tables, throw food across the room and keep every customer fed. Serve enough orders to level up and build increasingly ridiculous abilities that turn a struggling waiter into a food-delivering machine.

But monsters don't wait forever.

Miss an order and your customers won't just leave a bad review. They can throw things at you, slap you around, cover the floor in hazards or simply decide that you look better than what’s on the menu.

Build your waiter

Every run gives you new upgrades, relics and combinations.

Carry more dishes. Dash through tables while automatically serving customers. Ricochet plates between hungry monsters. Surround yourself with flying food. Turn dropped meals into automatic deliveries.

Combine upgrades and discover powerful builds that completely change how you serve the restaurant.

Every monster is a problem to solve

Customers have different appetites, personalities and behaviors.

Some are impatient. Some order huge meals. Some create hazards when they get angry. Others change their order or demand several dishes at once.

The longer they wait, the more dangerous the restaurant becomes.

Survive the full shift

A full run takes you through three increasingly dangerous restaurants.

Spend around 10 minutes surviving each location, defeat its boss and move to the next area while keeping your build.

Each restaurant introduces a new layout, visual theme, enemies and challenges.

Reach the third location and face the final mega-customer.

Feed it before it feeds on you.

Features

  • Fast action roguelike gameplay built around serving monsters

  • Random upgrades, relics and powerful build synergies

  • Throw food, dash between tables and chain deliveries

  • Monster customers with different orders, traits and attacks

  • Three distinct restaurant locations in one full run

  • Boss customers and a final mega-boss

  • Slapstick punishments and unique ways to get eaten

  • Permanent progression and unlocks between runs

  • Cute-dark visuals with chaotic monster comedy

Cross-play with the Nintendo Switch version. CPU players fill any empty seats, so you can jump in solo anytime.

To hide a tree, use a forest. To hide a person, use a crowd.

The streets of Tokyo. A hundred people crossing an intersection, waiting on a platform...

Walking, stopping, checking their phones.

Three fugitives - the VECTOR - are somewhere in there.

Their goal is simple: slip past the hunters, the ONI, and reach the exit.

Run and you stand out. Stop and you look suspicious.

Can you become just another face in the crowd?

One clue only. Check it against the poster!

The wanted poster the ONI carry lists two traits of a single fugitive.

"Black hair." "Wearing glasses." That is all.

Plenty of pedestrians match both. They are everywhere.

Question them one by one. Narrow it down. Get it wrong.

Then keep going.

The VECTOR can swap appearances!?

The VECTOR can trade looks with anyone in the crowd.

Become someone else before they close in, and walk away clean.

But you will be reported, and the poster will be updated.

Getting caught is not the end.

A captured VECTOR is escorted away and locked in a cage.

Even then, it is not over. Their teammates can come for them.

Leave them behind and run, or take the risk and break them out.

And ONI - do not relax once the cage is shut.

Turn around and it may already be empty...

How to play

Online play for up to 6 players at once.

You can also create private rooms that only people who know the code can join.

If you're short on players, CPUs fill the empty seats, so whether you're playing solo or with a friend, you can jump in whenever you like.

Two teams of three play two rounds, and the higher total score wins.

Roles switch every round - VECTOR one round, ONI the next.

Master both sides and carry your team.

At a glance

  • Asymmetric 3v3 — up to six players online, or play against CPU

  • A crowd of 100 — cover, witnesses and obstacles, all at once

  • Only two traits to go on — and plenty of pedestrians fit them

  • Swap your appearance — the only way to break a chase

  • Jail and rescue — write them off, or go back for them

  • Sides switch at halftime — play both roles in one match

  • Passphrase rooms — play with people you know

  • Cross-play — play together with the Nintendo Switch version

An internet connection is required for online play.

Video and streaming

Videos, live streams and clips are welcome. Monetise them freely. No permission and no notice are needed.

Put "TOKYO WANTED" in the title or the description, and the people watching can find their way here.

Passphrases are masked by default, and a passphrase you reveal hides itself again after 20 seconds. Leave one on screen and forget about it — viewers still cannot walk into your room.

Want your viewers to play with you? Share the passphrase in chat and up to six of you can play together. The free demo works the same way.

"Experiment 4051 begins. I wiped the previous 4050 into the stairwell." - the Tower

ONE TOWER. TWO KNIGHTS. NO PATIENCE.

Two of you, one screen, one very rude tower. Every floor runs on a clock: hold out while the Tower grows impatient and the horde grows hungrier, then take the stairs. Twenty floors to the Tower's mouth. Win, and HELL opens below - and HELL keeps going. Solo works too - the Tower just has more time for you.

YOUR WEAPONS FIRE THEMSELVES

You never click to attack. You move, you dash, you drag your partner out of the fire. 20 weapons, from a CLUB to an actual FISH - and picking the same one again evolves it. Swear an OATH before you climb: the Butcher's axe, the Archer's bow, the Shadow's dagger. One weapon, one rule, and a cape to match - or, in co-op, swear BLOOD BROTHERS together and share every wound. Carry the right catalyst and every one of them awakens into something new.

BUILDS THAT GET STUPID

Stack five copies of an EFFECT card and it stops being an item: STORM RING becomes LIGHTNING ROD, BLAST FIST becomes FUSE FIST. Keep stacking it - EFFECT cards have no cap. Stand close to your partner and your builds fuse.
"That is not a build anymore. That is weather." - the Tower

EVERY ZONE IS A PLACE

A cold rotunda with an arcade and a medallion. A long UNCANNY nave of arches and lit niches. A SICK ward crowned around a bottomless well. A NIGHTMARE cross built around a rose medallion. And HELL - the burned twin of the first hall, with the Tower's core beating at its heart. Most floors have their ruin - a crashed chandelier, a toppled monument, a memorial built from the weapons of climbers before you - and on the SICK and NIGHTMARE floors, the Tower has already started to digest it.

On many floors, low stone screens shape the fight: hop over them while the horde has to go around, and let the stone eat the shots aimed at you. A Warden guards every fifth floor, drawn from its zone's pool of five, so the four you meet change from climb to climb - and THE COLLECTOR shows up carrying copies of your own weapons.

ONE MORE CLIMB

Beat the Tower to open the next of five DEPTHS. 51 dares unlock new weapons, oaths and cards; Wardens hand out ten legendary relics; and the walls hide more than stone. Your deepest climb goes on the Steam leaderboards - solo, co-op, friends and TODAY'S TOWER.

WHAT'S IN THE BOX

  • Couch co-op on one PC: split-screen with two gamepads, a gamepad and the keyboard, or one shared keyboard
  • Play together online with Steam Remote Play Together - only one of you needs the game
  • Four modes, including DAILY TOWER and DUEL (couch PvP, first one down loses)
  • Full controller support, 15 languages
  • Steam leaderboards: solo, co-op, friends and a daily board for TODAY'S TOWER
  • Early Access: fully playable today; more deep-floor monsters and Wardens are on the way


"They're one floor up. They're always one floor up. I make sure of it." - the Tower

Add it to your wishlist and Steam will notify you the moment it's out.

Your towers become the walls

TOWER TOWER is a tower defense game about stacking.

The blocks you buy fall from the top of the screen and pile up on the terrain, forming your towers. Cannons and lasers are not simply placed — they are stacked. And what you stack becomes a wall that physically bends the enemy's route.

Stack higher, and the path twists further. The shape of your defense line is your strategy.




Stack. Mislead. Wipe them out.

Attack blocks are not your only weapons. Blocks with no attack power are cheap to place and work as terrain for steering how enemies move.

・Wall them off and force the long way around

・Build a V shape and gather them into one spot

・Build a lattice and make them wander the maze

・Hit the crowd with area damage once they gather

Where you stack, and what you stack. That alone changes the difficulty of the same wave completely.

An arsenal chosen by the numbers

Every block differs in cost, attack power, cooldown, range, anti-air capability and blast radius, and every block can be upgraded. Compare the numbers and combine them according to the role each part of your line has to play.

ABOUT THIS GAME

TOX-17 is a detective and investigation game where you analyze real video footage to uncover the truth behind mysterious incidents.

In the first case, an unknown person injects a strange substance into a product at a local market and disappears without a trace. The only evidence left behind is a collection of video recordings.

Your task is to carefully examine every clip, identify hidden clues, and follow the trail step by step.

Investigate:

• The country shown in the footage
• The city where the events take place
• The neighborhood and street
• The final location connected to the case

Every detail matters. Signs, architecture, vehicles, symbols, landmarks, and environmental clues can all lead you closer to the truth.

Features:

• Real video footage (FMV) investigation gameplay
• Multi-stage location deduction system
• Video controls for pausing, rewinding, and frame-by-frame analysis
• Note-taking and clue tracking mechanics
• Multiple hidden clues in every case
• Single-player detective experience

Observe carefully, connect the evidence, and uncover the truth behind TOX-17.

WARDEN CONTRACT: ACTIVE

Something came through the Rift. WARDEN has four operatives on the payroll and an

equipment requisition budget.

TROUBLE SHOOTERS is a 2D roguelite run-and-gun. Every run assembles a fresh chain of

rooms, hands you whatever the drop tables felt like handing you, and asks you to make it

work. The aliens are numerous, expressive, and extremely committed. So are you.

FOUR OPERATIVES

  • GRUNT — Rifle, no surprises, no bad matchups. Being good at everything turns

    out to be worth a great deal.

  • TANK — Fights with pile-driver fists and closes distance like it is a

    personal matter. An unstoppable force, not an immovable object.

  • DOC — Combat tech with a drone escort. Keeps a squad upright.

    Working alone, he remains optimistic.

  • WRAITH — Dagger spray, frenzy, no margin for error. The highest damage

    on the roster attached to the thinnest skin on the roster.

YOUR DSCO CARRIES THE BIG GUN

Field weapons do not go in your hands. They go to your DSCO — a Deployable Support Combat

Operator, which is a drone that follows you, holds the weapon, and fires when you fire.

Pick up a railgun and the drone brings it along until the ammunition runs out, then drops

it and waits for the next one. Your own weapon never runs dry, so you are never unarmed

and never stuck with a bad pickup.

GEAR THAT COMPOUNDS

Over sixty stacking items, plus consumables for when the plan stops working. Effects

multiply rather than replace. A run that begins with a slightly faster reload can end with

a screen that is no longer strictly legible.

FIVE BOSSES

Every zone ends with something that takes up the whole screen. The Foremen are four

industrial androids working a shared metronome, attacking in sequence — and the sequence

tightens every time one of them goes down. The others are worse.

2-4 PLAYER CO-OP

Bring a squad. A death is not the end of the run while a teammate is still standing: you are

listed as a casualty and redeploy at the next zone boundary. The run only ends when the

last operative goes down.

FOUR OPERATION TIERS

Easy through INVADERS MUST DIE, each one unlocked by finishing the one before it. At the

Build your own television empire in TV Station Tycoon, a management game where every show, schedule, advertisement, and business decision can change your position in the ratings.

Start with a small station and turn it into a broadcasting powerhouse. License new programs, build daily schedules, target different audiences, secure sponsors, manage your finances, and react to changing viewer habits as you compete against rival networks.

Build the Perfect Schedule

Your programming lineup is the heart of your station. Choose what to broadcast and when, balancing genres, audience demographics, popularity, costs, and time slots.

Morning news might perform well with one audience, while cartoons, sports, reality shows, dramas, movies, and late-night programming attract completely different viewers.

A strong schedule can create momentum throughout the day. A poor one can send viewers straight to the competition.

License and Manage Content

Expand your library by licensing television shows, movies, special events, and seasonal programming.

Every piece of content has its own strengths, audience appeal, popularity, runtime, and licensing cost. Look for bargains, invest in proven hits, or take a chance on cheaper programming that could become the foundation of your station.

Some opportunities are limited, so deciding when to spend your budget can be just as important as deciding what to broadcast.

Fight for the Ratings

Your audience changes throughout the day.

Viewer numbers are influenced by your programming, time slot, target demographic, weather, competing stations, previous shows, special events, and other factors.

Follow your live audience, study performance data, and adjust your strategy to climb the national rankings.

Your goal is simple: become the #1 television station.

Make Money From Your Audience

Ratings alone will not keep the lights on.

Turn your audience into revenue through advertising, sponsorships, and smart financial management. Bigger shows can attract more viewers, but they also cost more to license and operate.

Decide when to invest, when to save, and when to take a risk on content that could transform your station.

Grow Your Broadcasting Empire

As your station becomes more successful, unlock new opportunities and improve the way your network operates.

Manage your content library, advertising strategy, audience, finances, studio operations, campaigns, syndication opportunities, and competition from one growing broadcasting business.

Features

  • Build and manage your own TV station

  • Create full daily and weekly broadcast schedules

  • License shows, movies, sports, news, reality TV, cartoons, and more

  • Track live viewers and audience demographics

  • Compete against rival television networks

  • Climb the national ratings

  • Manage advertising and sponsorship deals

  • Monitor revenue, expenses, and station performance

  • Take advantage of seasonal content and limited-time broadcast events

  • React to weather and changing audience behavior

  • Analyze the performance of individual programs

  • Develop your station from a small broadcaster into a major network

A Personal Note

TV Station Tycoon was inspired in part by Mad TV, a game I loved playing when I was younger. I always wanted to return to the idea of running a television station, but with a much deeper focus on economics, management, strategy, and the small decisions behind keeping a broadcasting business alive.

I'm also a lifelong fan of tycoon and management games. I've been playing them since the Commodore 64 era and have spent decades trying almost every management game I could get my hands on.

With TV Station Tycoon, I wanted to create the kind of game I personally enjoy: a detailed management simulator where schedules, finances, ratings, viewers, competitors, and dozens of small decisions all interact.

If you enjoy digging into numbers, optimizing systems, experimenting with strategies, and slowly turning a struggling business into an empire, I hope you'll feel at home here.

Every hour matters.

Choose the right programs, understand your viewers, beat your competitors, and build a television network that millions want to watch.

YOU COMMAND THE ARMY, NOT A HERO

Most deckbuilders hand you one fighter and a stack of verbs. Table of War hands you a company.

Your units move and fight on their own action points — walk them, flank them, hold a ridge with them, no card required. The deck sits on top of that as your command channel: reinforcements, ordnance, standing orders, structures, and the fuel for your general's signature power. Two systems, two jobs. The board is the tactics. The deck is the strategy.

EVERY SOLDIER HAS A NAME

Your roster is persistent and it is permanent. Troops carry their name, rank, experience and scars from battle to battle, promote through a branch-specific rank ladder, and earn permanent perks at camps.

They do not come back. A rifleman you have carried since Act 1 — three promotions, a medal, a nickname you gave him yourself — dies to one badly-read artillery arc, and the next battle starts without him. The run economy is built around that: survivors carry forward, salvage buys what you can afford to replace, and every reckless push is a decision about who you can stand to lose.

THE BOARD FIGHTS BACK

Battles are fought on procedurally generated, non-rectangular maps — eight silhouettes carved out of void, so no two fronts have the same shape.

  • Zones of control — you cannot sprint past an armed enemy. Lines have to be broken, not dodged.

  • Flanking — a second body adjacent to the target, not to you. Positioning is a two-unit problem.

  • Fog of war — with a movement rule that stops you sleepwalking into the dark.

  • Terrain and cover — forest, hills, water and rock; some of it carveable, most of it not.

  • Environmental hazards — inferno, toxic, mire and EMP fields, plus drifting storms that wander the board and hurt whoever is standing in them. Including the enemy. There is a whole pacifist toolkit built on that fact.

  • Friendly fire — artillery splashes. It does not check whose uniform it is landing on.

  • Objectives that are not "kill everything" — survive N turns, hold a position under contest.

  • Raiders — a fast thief that crashes a skirmish, grabs your salvage and runs for the map edge. Kill it before it gets there or the money is gone for good.

And you can see it coming. Enemy intent is telegraphed on your turn: ghosted enemy positions, projected attack arrows, damage numbers, and a two-tier danger overlay separating "they can reach here" from "they can shoot you from here" — all of it updating live as you move. Turn it on, turn any layer of it off, play it blind if you want the fear.

THREE COMMANDERS, THREE DIFFERENT GAMES

  • The Warlord — cheap reinforcements and a Wrath gauge that fills on every kill and every loss. Spend it on Rally the Horde: two free riflemen, deployed at the front, right now.

  • The Engineer — the first structure each turn is free, and adjacent power plants charge a gauge that fires Overcharge: every turret double-fires, command points surge, damage repairs.

  • The Nomad — the HQ is a vehicle. There is no fixed base to defend because there is no fixed base. Movement builds Momentum; spend it on Break Camp and the whole army acts again.

Each brings its own starting army, deck skew, and around thirty exclusive cards nobody else can draft.

BUILD A RUN THAT BREAKS THE GAME

  • 176 cards across six categories, 100 of them commander-exclusive, nearly all upgradeable.

  • 38 relics with compounding effects — and eight of them are cursed, which you will find out.

  • 56 events with real double-edged choices, some gated behind relics you are carrying.

  • Curses the enemy injects into your own deck, removable only at an Outpost, for a price.

  • Four acts — First Contact, Two Fronts, Encirclement, Conquest — on a branching node map with seven node types.

  • Nine hand-authored bosses, each with its own mechanic: endless waves, halved damage unless you flank, a curse every single turn, and one that changes the rules at half health.

  • Fourteen elite variants and five enemy archetypes that reshape a battle before it starts, and tell you which one you are facing before you commit.

THEN RAISE THE STAKES

Twelve rungs of Ascension, each stacking one more rule on top of the last, themes rotating as you climb. Seven run modifiers you can stack yourself for score. A Daily Commission everyone plays on the same seed. Fifty-seven achievements, sixteen collectible board chips, and a seeded-run field so you can hand somebody an exact run and dare them.

AT A GLANCE

  • 3 commanders · 4-act branching expedition · 7 node types · permadeath roster

  • 176 cards · 38 relics · 56 events · 57 achievements · 12 ascension rungs · 7 run modifiers

  • 33 unit and structure classes · 14 elite variants · 5 enemy archetypes · 9 bosses

  • Procedural non-rectangular battlefields · fog of war · zones of control · hazards · friendly fire

  • Seeded runs · Daily Commission · save and resume between battles

  • Fully offline. No account, no launcher, no telemetry, no ads, nothing to buy.

Turn your love for tabletop games into a thriving business, where every shelf, dice, and customer tells a story.

Stock your shelves, host board game sessions, craft your own games, and build a shop loved by collectors and gamers alike.

Sell themed figures to complete collections and unlock unique dioramas and rewards. Completed collections increase your shop's appeal and value.

Set up game tables, craft your own board games from collected components, and host play sessions to earn extra income and attract dedicated players.

Build, move, and arrange your shelves the way you like.

Design a layout that fits your style and keeps your store efficient.

Unpack deliveries and place your products with care.

Organize your inventory smartly to keep customers happy and your store efficient.

Level up to unlock new licenses, products, and expand your shop.

Each level brings fresh opportunities and deeper gameplay.

Don’t let the mess drive customers away.

Use your mop to keep the store spotless and earn cleaner feedback.

Smelly store? Customers won’t stay long.

Use sprays and fans to remove odor and maintain a fresh shopping environment.

Keep the game tables clean between sessions.

A tidy environment makes your store the perfect hangout spot.

More Features

Every journey begins the same.

A zombie outbreak has devastated the world. You leave your home and set out for the Port, hoping to board the last evacuation ship.

But everything that happens along the way is different.

Random event cards constantly reshape your adventure. You may rescue a stranger, fall into an ambush, discover precious supplies, or find yourself trapped by a single bad decision.

Every playthrough tells a new story.

Choice

There are no easy answers at the end of the world.

Will you share your last supplies with a complete stranger?

Will you risk your life to protect someone being bullied by raiders?

Will you abandon a badly wounded companion to save food and water?

Every choice changes the course of your story and ultimately your fate.

Resources

Water, food, medicine, and ammunition are all desperately scarce. Even a good night’s sleep or a moment of entertainment becomes a luxury.

Carefully manage every resource you can find, maintain your health, and keep your mood up.

Sometimes, people don't die because the enemy is stronger.

They die from exhaustion and despair.

Team

Throughout your journey, you’ll meet new survivors, each with randomly generated attributes and skills.

Build your team wisely and make the most of everyone’s strengths if you hope to survive.

Every playthrough brings different companions, and together you'll forge your own story through the apocalypse.

Equipment

Trade with merchants, scavenge fallen enemies, repair damaged gear, and upgrade your weapons and armor to face ever greater dangers.

In the apocalypse, quality equipment is hard to come by.

Sometimes, an ordinary shovel is all that stands between you and death.

Combat

Unlike traditional card battles, the Card Distance system gives weapon range real tactical significance.

The Entanglement system allows melee weapons to truly shine, making knives far more dangerous than machine guns once combat enters the Entangled State.

Combine each weapon's strengths with smart positioning to develop tactics that are uniquely your own.

Customize the Rules

Reduced shooting accuracy at night?

Food spoils over time?

Gunfire attracts zombies?

…

Customize the survival rules of the apocalypse and create the challenge you want to face.

It All Started as a Tabletop Experiment

This game began as a simple tabletop experiment.

I wanted to find out whether a deck of random event cards could create a different story every time it was played. The results exceeded my expectations. Compared with traditional RPGs built around a fixed storyline, the unpredictability of completely random adventures created a far more memorable experience.

After years of refining that idea, it eventually became Tabletop Survivors.

Every journey is different.

Every choice matters.

Every playthrough tells a new story.

Tabletop TD is a random tower defense where everyone sits around a tavern table and defends their own board. Survive 30 waves to clear the game. If enemies fill your board, you lose.



  • 5 ages and 30 waves, from Primitive to Future
  • Fast, air, armored and splitting enemies
  • A timed boss at the end of each age
  • The board changes with each age
  • Older towers deal less damage to enemies from newer ages
  • Endless mode with no final wave



  • Spend gold to draw random towers
  • 30 towers across 5 ages
  • 6 roles: single-target, splash, support, anti-air, chain and mark
  • A small chance to draw towers from later ages



  • Merge 3 of the same tower to raise its grade, with no chance of failure
  • Use 1 tower and 2 gems in place of 3 towers
  • Every tower gets its own trait at top grade
  • Combine 3 towers to craft special units
  • Rune stones add new effects in Endless mode
  • Sell towers you don't need for gold



  • Place towers freely on open spots on the board
  • Drag from the overhead view and move groups at once
  • Carry or throw towers by hand in first person



  • Solo or online co-op for up to 4 players
  • Voice chat in the lobby and during the game
  • Place your towers on a teammate's board
  • Team missions with rewards for the whole table

Between waves, you can walk around the tavern. Grab a beer, hit the punching bag, play the slot machine and the gacha machine, or drop-kick the bartender.

Light the Taiji, lay out the Bagua, and let Tarot answer.

Once a day, three minutes — a ritual made only for today.

HOW IT WORKS

Step into the Bagua layout and touch the Taiji at its center to begin. Across

three rounds — Heaven, Human Affairs, and Foundation — you'll choose 8 cards

from a rotating hand of 5, guided by instinct rather than logic.

Your reading is shaped by an original three-layer interpretation system: a primary palace

sets the tone, a secondary palace tempers it, and reversed cards add their own

shade of meaning. The result isn't a single line — it's a short passage covering

tone, guidance, energy, and a small note of encouragement, unique to your day.

NINE PATHS TO ASK

Choose what you want to reflect on: General, Love, Career, Wealth, Health,

Relationships, Study, Decisions, or Travel. Each path allows one "official"

reading per day — additional draws become playful, unrecorded readings, so the

ritual never turns into grinding.

TWENTY-EIGHT CARDS, EIGHT PALACES

The deck blends 20 classic Tarot cards with 8 original cards drawn from Chinese

myth and philosophy — Azure Dragon, White Tiger, Vermilion Bird, Black Tortoise,

and others — each placed deliberately within the Five Elements. Your draws land

across the eight palaces of the Bagua: Qian, Dui, Li, Zhen, Xun, Kan, Gen, Kun.

A QUIET, INK-WASH WORLD

Deep tones, gold accents, drifting ink fog, and a compass of stars frame every

reading. The soundtrack is minimal and meditative — closer to a solo guqin or

xiao than a game score — built for sitting with the result, not rushing past it.

RETURN, REFLECT, REMEMBER

Come back tomorrow and tell the app how yesterday's reading felt — spot on,

partial, or off. Your full history is saved and browsable, and 15 achievements

quietly track the shape of your practice over time, from a single visit to a

season of daily returns.

SHARE YOUR DAY

Turn any reading into a shareable card — a portrait-format keepsake of what the

cards said, ready to save or send.

Available in Chinese and English.

Tailor Hotel is a management simulation game where you build and run a one-of-a-kind hotel, transforming a 1st-floor lobby and the vast, empty spaces of the 2nd and 3rd floors into your dream establishment.

Design custom guest rooms from scratch, carefully placing beds, chairs, and decor to satisfy unique visitors with highly specific tastes.

Beyond room design, you'll step into the kitchen to whip up colorful room service orders on demand, serving guests quickly to boost their satisfaction.

Reinvest your hard-earned profits to expand your layout, unlock luxury furniture, and add premium amenities that elevate your hotel's reputation.

Bring your vision to life in Tailor Hotel and turn a modest building into a world-renowned destination for travelers everywhere!

  • You can accept room reservations and check booking statuses right from the monitor.

  • Order essential items and supplies whenever you need them.

  • Use the toolkit to install walls, doors, and lighting. Installing a door will reward you with its key.

  • Hand over the correct room key to arriving guests.

  • When room service orders come in, prepare the requested items from the order slip and deliver them to the room.

THE TIDE IS TAINTED

In 2032, humanity is on the brink of extinction.

The Tainted are mutating across land, sea, and sky, leaving destruction in their wake. The Stormfleet Expedition was humanity's chance to stop Whitepulse, the monster connected to this growing nightmare. But the mission has fallen apart, and soldier Riv Winters is left fighting for survival in a world where the ocean offers no refuge.

With a battered raft, limited supplies, and a mission that may cost him everything, Riv must survive the horrors of the open sea and make his way to Whitepulse alone on the Tainted Tide.

Welcome to Tainted Tide — a roguelite survival RPG combining resource management, crafting, match-3 combat, and bullet-hell.

SURVIVE ONE MORE DAY

Every day is a struggle between what you need now and what might save you later.

Your action points are limited. Food and water are scarce. Your raft is your lifeline, and every resource matters. Decide how to spend your day: fish for supplies, gather valuable materials, upgrade your equipment, or invest in your life raft's resource generators.

Every decision has consequences. A tempting reward might be worth the risk of an ambush, but a single mistake can leave you unprepared when night falls.

BUILD YOUR FLOATING LIFELINE

Your raft is more than a place to sleep. It is your workshop, your shelter, and your last line of defense.

Scavenge the remains of the old world and turn salvaged materials into a sustainable survival system. Upgrade your fishing equipment, water purifier, solar panels, salvage collector, and fish net to improve your daily income.

Manage your resources carefully, craft useful items and combat abilities, and prepare for the threats ahead.

MATCH, FIGHT, SURVIVE

The Tainted won't let you survive in peace.

Battle mutated creatures in a tactical match-3 combat system. Match colored orbs to generate mana, unleash abilities, manage your defenses, and exploit enemy weaknesses.

But choosing your attacks is only half the battle.

When enemies unleash their attacks, you must move, react, and dodge dangerous projectiles and attack patterns in real time. Learn their patterns, find your openings, and stay alive long enough to strike back.

CRAFT YOUR OWN WAY TO SURVIVAL

Strength alone won't save you. Preparation and the right combination of tools can make the difference between victory and another disastrous run.

  • Craft powerful abilities to expand your combat options.

  • Discover artifacts that grant valuable effects and advantages.

  • Develop your strategy around buffs, debuffs, shields, and damage-over-time effects.

  • Invest in permanent upgrades to strengthen future runs and push further into the unknown.

Adapt to the enemies you face, make the most of the resources you find, and build a strategy capable of surviving the horrors of the deep.

THE OCEAN HOLDS MORE THAN SECRETS

Strange signals, unexpected encounters, drifting supplies, and dangerous discoveries can change the course of your journey.

Each event presents a choice: take the risk for a potentially valuable reward, or turn away and live to fight another day. Traders and the remnants of the old world may offer opportunities.

YOUR MISSION ISN'T OVER

Deep beneath the waves, something monstrous awaits.

Every victory brings resources and experience. Every defeat teaches you something about the threats ahead. Keep improving your equipment, refine your skills, and become strong enough to face the horrors that stand between you and your mission.

Whitepulse still lives.

How much are you willing to sacrifice to give humanity a future?

The ancient beasts, the ascended immortals — all that remains of them now are scattered whispers and half-told tales.

Why did the gods and spirits vanish from the world? It all begins with a single broken god-realm.

You were not born to this world. The sovereign god Taiyi drew you into a small world he keeps for himself — a mortal, trapped upon a god’s game board. Fight battle after battle to uncover the truth of this realm, and find your way back to the mortal world.

A card’s growth goes far beyond a simple “level up”:

• Upgrade Paths — every card can grow along several routes; the choice is yours.

• Soul Enchant — bind extra effects onto a card until it transforms.

• Relics · Rewrite the Rules — relics don’t just boost numbers; they rewrite how the fight works.

• New Cards — unlock fresh cards along the way to deepen your pool.

The Martialist trades blows up close with fist, foot, and inner Qi; the Artificer keeps foes at bay with Luban contraptions and ammunition… Each class brings its own cards, skills, and gear — and its own way to survive.

Press deeper across the world map, where elites, bosses, events, and secrets wait in the mist for your choice. Every layer draws you closer to this world’s core — and the truth may weigh far heavier than “going home” ever did.

The heart of this game’s combat: battles don’t play out in a single row, but across a 3×3 grid — where positioning is strategy. Melee units hold the front line and soak damage; ranged fighters and summons hang back to blanket the field with fire. A single step can dodge a pit-fire, slip past a trap, or make an enemy’s heavy blow whiff. Foes maneuver too — read the red-cell attack zones, the spreading pit-fire, and the hidden mechanisms if you mean to have the last laugh.

It starts with your Spirit Root. Beyond the five Wu Xing roots — Metal, Wood, Water, Fire, Earth — six hidden roots await discovery on your journey. Each root has three tiers; the higher the tier, the more unusual the upgrade paths it unlocks. A root’s type and tier reshape the upgrade paths of most of your cards: the same card grows into a wholly different form under a different root. Your Spirit Root sets the course of the entire deck.
