Build a food-delivery empire, one scooter at a time.

Two delivery giants already own this city. You've got one scooter, an empty map, and a plan to take the whole thing.

Takeout Mania is a real-city food-delivery tycoon. Import a real place — genuine streets, genuine buildings — sign its restaurants, put couriers on the road, and out-hustle the competition order by order until the entire city orders through you.

🗺️ A real city, not a grid

Every map is a real location pulled from the world. The streets, intersections and buildings are the genuine article, and your couriers navigate the true road network with live routing. Type in your hometown and run your empire down roads you actually know — no two cities play the same.

🤝 Win it deal by deal

Independent restaurants are up for grabs. Negotiate commissions, sign them to your platform, and poach the ones already flying rival colors. It's a street-by-street tug-of-war with two entrenched giants — GrubWay and HyperEats — and on the largest cities, a third shark in the water.

🛵 Dispatch like an operator

Early on, every order is yours to run. Drag couriers onto jobs 911-Operator style, juggle a fickle freelancer pool, and keep the food moving before it goes cold. Hire full-timers and unlock auto-dispatch once you're ready to stop sweating every single delivery.

📣 Market or die

Nobody orders from an app they've forgotten. Blanket districts with flyers, raise billboards, target specific neighborhoods with social campaigns, and run voucher, referral and spotlight promos. Awareness always fades — the marketing never stops.

🏙️ A city that lives without you

Households have budgets, cravings and daily rhythms. Restaurants open where demand runs hot, thrive on good reviews, franchise across town — or go bankrupt and leave a vacant unit for the next dreamer. From shawarma joints and pizzerias to sushi bars, delis and fine dining — 12 venue types, plus groceries and banks that will happily lend you the rope.

🎲 Trouble on the road

36 random incidents keep every run honest — a slammed kitchen, a food influencer at the door, a spilled drink, an allergy scare. There are no clean answers, only trade-offs: which stat can you afford to lose, and which one do you want to win?

🏢 From scooter to empire

Hit 100 reputation and found your headquarters, then choose the traits that define your operation: full-time hiring, marketing muscle, ghost kitchens that cook the cuisines you can't sign, auto-dispatch, customer support, sharper negotiators. Rent vacant units, open your own restaurants, and franchise your name across the map.

Features at a glance

  • Play a real city — anywhere on Earth
  • Couriers that ride the actual road network with live routing
  • Sign, negotiate and poach restaurants from two+ AI rivals
  • Hands-on 911-Operator dispatch, or automate it at scale
  • Deep marketing: flyers, billboards, targeted social, campaigns
  • A living economy of households, reviews, franchises and bankruptcies
  • 12 venue types, plus groceries and banks
  • 36 trade-off order events
  • Build an HQ and specialize with strategic traits
  • €/$/£ currencies and adjustable starting capital

Wishlist Takeout Mania and start your first shift.

Adventure & Combat

Tale Sweeper is a casual incremental adventure game. Move your cursor to auto-attack enemies within range while skills cast automatically!

Loot & Gathering

Defeating monsters and completing quests yields materials and gold, with a rare chance to drop powerful Artifacts and Orbs.

Skill Tree

Spend materials and gold to unlock skills that grant new abilities, massive stat boosts, and maximum clearing efficiency!

Shop

Spend gold on potions that auto-activate during combat, granting powerful buffs to keep you going.

Forge

Craft brand-new weapons using materials. Upgrades not only boost your stats but also expand your attack range.

Orbs

Once your weapon reaches a certain level, rare Orbs will begin to drop. Orbs provide stat bonuses and can even alter your attack style.

Artifacts

Artifacts provide unique passive abilities. Equip up to three per battle to create powerful, game-changing synergies!

1592—A War Where Magic and Steel Collide

1592. You may remember the year from a history lesson long ago.

But this time, magic exists on the battlefield—and the enemy you fought yesterday may stand beside you as an ally today.

Tale of Specters: Joseon 1592 is an alternate-history fantasy tactical RPG set during the Imjin War. Lead a ragtag company of exiles, surrendered soldiers, and outlaws across a war-torn Joseon where magic and steel share the battlefield.

Win Through Tactics, Not Numbers Alone

Victory depends on more than raw stats.

Every battlefield is designed around elevation and terrain. Seize the high ground, force enemies into unfavorable positions, and turn the landscape itself into a weapon.

Exploit the relationships between the four elements—Earth, Water, Fire, and Wind—while carefully tracking the turn order. Combine skills with the right status effects, and even a seemingly hopeless battle can become a hard-earned victory.

A Three-Tier Class Progression System: 8 → 12 → 8

Build your company through a three-tier class system, beginning with 8 basic classes and progressing into 12 intermediate and 8 advanced classes.

The same character can fulfill an entirely different role depending on their class, skills, and place within your formation.

Salvage, Reforge, and Customize Your Equipment

Your equipment can be developed just as deeply as your soldiers.

Imbue weapons with elemental properties, raise their grade, or dismantle battlefield loot at the forge and rebuild it into something more useful. Create equipment combinations tailored to your company and preferred tactics.

Recruit Figures from History and Legend

Meet Hong Sa-heon, a commander hiding his past; Lee Dong-gil, a lowborn mage whose spells can reshape the battlefield; Maechang, a gisaeng and poet more skilled with a blade than a brush; and Heo Gyun, the scholar credited with writing The Tale of Hong Gildong.

Recruit characters with distinct histories, personalities, and abilities—and bring them together under your command.

Turn Yesterday’s Enemies into Today’s Allies

Victory does not always have to end with your enemy’s death.

Persuade defeated foes to join your company, then turn former opponents into key assets in the battles ahead. Win, recruit, reorganize your forces, and take on ever-greater challenges.

Three difficulty settings allow both newcomers and experienced tactical RPG players to enjoy the game at their preferred level of challenge.

Current Development Status

Tale of Specters: Joseon 1592 will enter Early Access with its core systems in place, alongside four chapters containing a total of 50 stages.

We plan to continue expanding the game with additional content and features while incorporating feedback from our players throughout Early Access.

The price will increase when the game reaches its full 1.0 release.

One word can change a story

An unfamiliar study. A locked door. A voice calling for help from a book. Turn your own name into a keyword and begin changing the book's sentences.

Tale'Switch is a puzzle adventure about placing keywords into the sentences of a book. Take keywords discovered through reading and investigation into other tales. Deduce the properties of objects, change the words of a sentence, and find a new ending for a story that has reached a dead end.

Read, investigate, and connect

  • Change sentences and read scenes shaped by the keywords you choose.
  • Unfold locations as pop-up books and investigate them for clues.
  • Compare short object records to deduce how each keyword can be used.
  • Collect characters' names from notes left on the bookshelf and discover connections between tales from different genres.

The witch's story remains locked. Where will you find the word that completes its sentence?

THE ULTIMATE TANK PARTY GAME

Grab a controller, call your friends and get ready for chaos. Tank Them All is a fast top-down party game for 2–6 players: six tanks enter, one hit is enough, and only one tank rolls out. Rounds are short, everybody is back in the next one, and a new arena loads every round — so “just one more match” turns into the whole evening.

PERFECT FOR GAME NIGHT

  • Couch multiplayer — up to 6 players on one screen, with gamepads or keyboard
  • Online with friends — create a room and share the code, or jump into an open lobby
  • Remote Play Together — invite Steam friends into your local game, only one copy needed
  • Bots fill every empty seat — and they adapt to every game mode
  • Easy to pick up — one stick to move, one button to fire; anyone can join in seconds

4 GAME MODES. ENDLESS CHAOS.

⚔ Free For All

Pure, unfiltered mayhem. Last tank rolling wins. Set your own rules — play by rounds or rack up kills.

🤝 Team Battle

Two teams, one winner. Revive fallen teammates with the Repair power-up and coordinate fire — friendly fire is OFF, but accidents happen.

🏆 King of the Hill

A glowing zone appears on the arena. Hold it. Score points every second you're inside. But the zone shrinks — and moves. Respawn, adapt, survive.

🐚 Golden Shell

One golden shell drops somewhere on the map. Pick it up and you become the most dangerous — and most hunted — tank on the battlefield. Score points every second you hold it. Kill while holding for a bonus. Die and it's gone.

16 POWER-UPS. INFINITE COMBINATIONS.

Collect up to 3 power-ups simultaneously and stack brutal combinations:

  • Homing Missile— locks on and chases enemies

  • Bounce Bullet — ricochets off walls to hit from impossible angles

  • Boomerang — fires forward, curves back, hits twice

  • Explosion Shell — area-damage devastation

  • Nitro — speed boost to chase or escape

  • Shield — absorbs one lethal hit

  • Ice Path — leave a slippery trail that disrupts enemies

  • Dash Killer — your dash becomes a lethal weapon

  • Artillery — call in a strike from above

  • Mine — plant traps and control the arena

  • Electric Shot — zaps every tank around the impact: stunned, with reversed controls

  • Fire Shell — leaves a trail of flames in its wake

  • Grenade Launcher — every hit scatters grenades all around

  • Rapid Fire — two shells in the air at once

  • Double Dash — hold the dash for a long-range lunge

  • Repair — bring fallen teammates back into the fight

THE ARENA FIGHTS BACK.

Surviving other players isn't enough. Every match can bring:

  • ☁ Poison Cloud — deadly gas closes in from the edges

  • 💣 Minefield — the battlefield perimeter becomes a death zone

  • 🌪 Tornado — weather turns violent during storms

  • ✈ Air Raid — bombs fall from the sky at timed intervals

…and the arenas themselves are rigged:

  • 🔪 Spike Walls — step on the wrong plate and a wall of spikes slams out

  • ⚙ Spinning Blades — spiked blades sweep everything in their path

  • 🌊 Deep Water — one careless move and your tank sinks to the bottom

  • 🔥 Burning Trees — a stray shot can set the forest ablaze

  • 🌀 Portals — warp across the arena in a blink

90+ ARENAS. NEVER THE SAME MATCH TWICE.

Sand dunes. Dense jungles. Tropical islands linked by rickety bridges. Brick mazes, junkyards and crystal fields. Each arena is a different battlefield — different cover, different flow, different strategy. A new arena is loaded every round.

QUICK TO LEARN. HARD TO MASTER.

One stick to move. One button to charge and fire. Then it gets complicated — in the best possible way.

These are not pets. They are specimens.

In Tank of the Fittest, you take control of an industrial aquarium on the edge of collapse. Twist heat, pH, oxygen, and pollution to create deliberate survival pressure, then watch ordinary fish become casualties, predators, or evolving anomalies.

Turn the tank into a selection engine

The environment is not a comfort checklist. It is your primary tool. Raise the heat, shift the pH, starve the water of oxygen, or let pollution spread to drive different specimens toward different outcomes.

Make death part of the experiment

The weak leave behind food and biological material. Their remains attract scavengers, feed predators, alter pollution, and keep the ecosystem moving. One death can strengthen a hunter or tip the entire tank into a new collapse.

Build around the survivors

Specimens gain traits, form synergies, and follow distinct evolution paths in response to clear, predictable pressures. Commit to a few focused build paths and turn one survivor into an apex specimen dangerous enough to dominate the entire tank.

Archive what the tank creates

Advance the experiment through tasks, unlock new fish lineages in the Mutation Codex, and record the specimens and traits you discover. Archive the results of each run and turn unfinished discoveries into goals for the next experiment.

  • Control heat, pH, oxygen, and pollution
  • Watch pursuit, escape, devouring, scavenging, and evolution form ecosystem chains
  • Build key specimens around trait families and synergies
  • Unlock 15 base fish lineages and record 45 specimen forms
  • Explore 117 obtainable traits and 36 synergies

Your garden has a pest problem. You have a swatter.

TapTrapGrow mixes arcade action with incremental progression: short hunts, permanent upgrades and a garden that gets busier as you grow stronger. Guide your swatter, earn gold and turn a well-placed hit into a chain reaction.

Light it up. Let the shells fly.


Start in the dark and throw Flash glow sticks to reveal nearby pests. Your swatter swings automatically; you guide it with the mouse. Unlock permanent garden lighting, then smack turtle shells into the swarm and keep them ricocheting.

More pests. Bigger reactions.


Discover six species and unlock their Bomb, Frost, Poison and Electric variants. Set off explosions, freeze crowds, spread poison and send sparks between targets. Spend gold on permanent upgrades, pest populations and gold rewards. Complete hunt goals to improve your attack power, speed and elemental effects.

Keep your eyes on the cake


Once the permanent lights are on, two cakes need defending. Swat thieves before they escape with a slice. The more cake you save, the bigger your gold bonus at the end of the hunt.

Lure fireflies into your glow-stick light and catch them for temporary shell boosts or crystals. Bigger shells, shells that keep moving, and cake thieves on the run give you plenty to aim for.

Six bosses. One last garden showdown.


Defeat each species' boss to unlock the finale, where all six return together. Bring down every boss and keep at least half the cake slices safe until time runs out. After victory, you can play the finale again.

A single-player garden rampage, one stronger run at a time.

Tapis is a score-chasing roguelike that blends three pleasures: the luck of a draw, the strategy of chess-like placement, and building a poker hand that carries over from run to run. A tabletop game with a single goal, a higher score every time.

TAME THE TABLE

Every turn, the table fills with tokens, each with an effect that depends on its position and its family. Trigger your mover tokens to swap, push and reposition the pieces, and turn a simple draw into a cascade of points.

Then hit score. Tokens fire one after another, multipliers stack up, and the history shows where every point came from. A single well placed token can take a board from a few dozen points to millions.

EQUIP YOUR HAND

Five playing cards make up your gear. Each grants an action to rearrange the table and a passive bonus you keep from one run to the next. Line up a flush, a pair, a straight, and your poker combinations empower entire families of tokens. It is up to you to build the perfect hand.

MANY PACKS, COUNTLESS STRATEGIES

Hundreds of tokens spread across themed packs: forest, river, sea, sky, mountain and more. Each pack brings its own wildlife, flora and mechanics. Play with multiple packs simultaneously to invent your own style.

Take the sea. Its tide tokens pull the water up from the bottom of the table, one row at a time, and the sea pulls back with every new draw unless something holds it. Some creatures grow stronger the deeper they sink, others wake up as the water recedes. How high you let the tide rise is up to you.

BUILT TO REPLAY

Clear six worlds in pursuit of the best score, then replay them in prestige for greater challenge and rewards. Take on the infinite mode and climb the leaderboard, or face the Survival mode.

In Survival mode, the table becomes a battlefield. Waves of creatures pour in, from a lone skirmisher to a five strong onslaught, each with its own nuisance: one gnaws at your charges, another siphons your points. Your score is your only weapon, so hold out as long as you can.

The next draw can change everything. Go all in.

TaskFall is an online co-op game, which features physics-based destruction, various missions, disasters, items and levels, each with their own unique gimmick. You and up to 3 friends will be assigned tasks by the Citadel, which you will have to complete, in order to extract home safely and get your pay.

Always watch your step!

Deadly catastrophes can strike your team at any given moment, turning every mission into a fight for survival. You never know what will come next, zombies? lava? UFOs??

Teamwork makes the dream work!

Stick together, coordinate under pressure, and rely on your crew to make it through the chaos...or at least comically fail to do so. And remember, a good employee follows protocol, a great one brings everybody home.

How will you adapt to the ever-changing environment?

Watch how the environments around you collapse while they are hit by the violent disasters and your teammates. A world is never left the same after the crew leaves it.

Heads up, trouble is always around you!

Complete the dangerous tasks assigned to your team by the Citadel and finish the job while trying your best to survive. With each mission completed, you will be assigned to a new and more difficult one.

Get only what is necessary!

Spend your hard-earned credits from the missions in the Citadel's shop. Buy new tools, items, and upgrades to prepare for what comes next. You are never overprepared.

  • Physics Based Destruction

  • Up to 4 Players Co-op

  • Emotes

  • Crazy Items

  • Multiple Handmade Levels With Unique Features

  • Various Disasters

  • Various Missions to Complete

  • Radio Item with Online and Local Music Support

  • Difficulty Scaling

  • Voice Chat

BUILD THE CHAIN. REACH CRITICAL MASS.

Tatomic is a high-energy falling-block puzzle game about building colorful atomic chains—and choosing the perfect moment to make them react.

Drop linked pairs into the containment field, rotate them into position, and connect atoms of the same element. Every element has its own critical mass. Reach it and the reaction travels through the chain one atom at a time, breaking supports, dropping everything above, and turning careful setups into spectacular cascades.

Build several chains together and trigger them in a single move for huge combo bonuses. The rules are easy to read. Surviving the pressure—and engineering the perfect reaction—is not.

THREE WAYS TO PLAY

Critical Mass

Climb through 30 escalating levels. Changing reaction thresholds and drop speeds force new strategies, while every level transforms the reactor with a distinct animated background and atom style.

Radioactive Survival

Radioactive atoms only detonate when they join a matching-color chain. Use them to prepare the board, choose when to trigger a reaction, and chase a high score as the pace accelerates.

Puzzle Mode

Reconstruct 20 authored molecular silhouettes using one exact connected chain. Shape, orientation, and atom count all matter—and radioactive hazards can destroy a nearly finished solution.

A REACTOR THAT RESPONDS TO EVERY MOVE

  • Chain-by-chain reaction propagation, unsupported-atom gravity, cascades, and simultaneous-chain combos

  • Thirty animated reactor environments with level-specific atom treatments

  • Element-specific explosions, particles, shockwaves, screen shake, and procedural sound effects

  • The restored original Tatomic soundtrack

  • A visible three-pair queue and ghost landing preview for deliberate play

  • Persistent high scores, records, run statistics, grades, and puzzle completion

  • First-run field training plus a replayable How to Play guide

  • Complete keyboard and controller navigation with controller-specific button glyphs

  • Steam Deck layout support, haptic feedback, and event-scaled controller rumble

  • Accessibility options for UI scale, audio channels, screen shake, motion, flashes, and color palettes

Tatomic revives the rules and three original modes of the classic game with a completely rebuilt native presentation made for modern PCs and handheld play.

On a small farm at the edge of the old woods, the crops keep vanishing and the farmer can't figure out why. He's not a bad farmer. He's just asleep when the trouble comes - and the trouble knows it.

But someone else has been watching. One night a Tomte, a whiskered little gnome out of Scandinavian folklore, crept down from the treeline and worked his magic on the farmer's scarecrow. That's you. The farmer still handles the planting, the watering, the harvest - he has no idea you can move. Everything that creeps out of the woods to eat his crops is your business now.

It won't be easy. The pests come in waves from first light to the dead of night, and the deeper the woods get stirred up, the stranger the things that wander out of them. But with a shed full of garden tools, a little folk magic, and maybe a friend or three, this old farm might have a future after all.

Features

Four shifts, no breaks. Deer and bunnies nibble at dawn, bears lumber in by afternoon, and after dark the woods send their strange ones - ghouls, mushroom goblins, and worse. The waves roll around the clock and grow with every day the farm survives.

Fight like a scarecrow. Send pests running with a wave of dread, or take a garden tool to them - trowel, hoe, rake, shovel, or a pitchfork that flings them clear across the field.

Build while they're coming. Dig trenches, set lures, plant stinging nettles, and raise spook stones right in the middle of the wave. The pests won't wait for you to get ready.

Leave notes for the farmer. Sign them "Ol' Jo," a helpful neighbor. He'll buy whatever seeds and tools the note suggests on his next market trip - as long as the harvest earned enough to cover it.

Sell crops or spend them. Whatever stays in the field, the farmer sells to keep the farm afloat. Whatever you quietly harvest yourself becomes crafting material. The farm's whole fate sits inside that choice.

Dig at your own risk. Five relics out of old folklore lie buried beneath the fields - a dwarf's ring, a pair of dancing shoes, and other things the stories warned about. Each one is powerful. Each one has a price, and you'll learn it the hard way.

Lose the farm, keep the lessons. When the farm is overrun, the fields reset - but the scarecrow remembers. Spend your hard-earned advancement points on permanent upgrades and get a little further each run.

Solo or 2-4 player online co-op. More scarecrows, more chaos - waves scale to the size of your crew.

The Magical Recipe Book

The heart of the game. It contains ingredient lists for dozens of potions. Some recipes are encrypted or require a strict sequence of actions. Communication is key: while one player holds the book and dictates the components for a "Potion of Flight," the other must scour the warehouse for mandrake root.

Serving Mythical Customers

You’ll be visited by everyone from fickle witches to furious forest spirits. If you serve the wrong potion, your guest won't just sit there in silence

Potion Effects and Progression

A successfully consumed potion triggers a visual effect on the client (size changes, glowing, levitation), earning you magical reputation and gold coins. Spend your gold to upgrade the tavern with faster cauldrons, automatic grinders, or new pages for your recipe book.

Obstacles

The kitchen is a hazardous place. Magical fumes might temporarily swap players' bodies or force them to move in reverse, demanding instant adaptation and seamless coordination.

Tavernia is an online board game for 2 to 8 players that mixes trivia with minigames. Answer questions to claim tiles on the board, and beat other players in minigames to take their tiles.



Answer a trivia question to claim an empty tile. There are thousands of questions on dozens of topics. To take another player's tile, play a minigame card and win the duel. If you lose your castle, you are out. The last player with a castle wins.




Build a deck of your five favourite minigames and ban the one you like least.

Perfect Circle: draw a rounder circle than your opponent.


Cartographer: put your pin closer to the city than your opponent.


Masterwork: finish the puzzle first.


Plus 17 more, including word games, typing races, rhythm games, mazes, lock picking and reaction tests.



  • Public and private rooms, plus Quick Match. Invite Steam friends from the lobby.
  • Streamers: connect Twitch or Kick. Your viewers can bet on duels and earn XP for their own accounts.
  • Watch any game live as a spectator
  • Level up, upgrade your cards to legendary, and collect hand skins and profile frames
  • English, Czech and German, with questions written for each language

Original music by Adam Sporka, composer on the Kingdom Come: Deliverance games.

Taxi Shift is a taxi simulator where knowing the city matters.

Rent a taxi, cover your shift costs, and try to finish the day with a profit. Wrong turns, wasted time, and poor route choices all cost money.

There is no GPS route line. Read the map, follow street signs, use landmarks, and learn the city as you drive.

As you progress, unlock new parts of the city and take on unfamiliar streets and routes.

TEACH MY LITTLE SISTER HOW TO DRIVE is a chaotic simulation game where you have to teach your sister who's driving on deadly roads.

Trapped in the passenger seat, the only thing you can do is to give proper directions to your sister through your voice. 

But remember, no matter what you scream, the wheel is still in her hands!

Real-Time Voice Conversations

Talk directly to your sister and teach her how to drive.

Give her driving instructions with your voice and watch her react to what you say in real time.

A Variety of Driving Courses

From beginner courses to actual road driving, the lessons only get harder.

The more comfortable your sister gets behind the wheel, the more you'll have to teach her.

Tough Driving Challenges 

The situations right in front of you will always be unpredictable.

Think fast, give clear instructions before your sister makes a mistake. 

Danger Around Every Corner

You never know what might happen on the road.

Customize Your Little Sister

Use customization options to make your sister look just like you.

Game Features

  • Voice-Driven Gameplay

  • An Annoying Little Sister

  • Passenger Seat Perspective

  • Bunch of Driving Missions

  • Character Customization

Inspired by I Didn't Cheat.

Text Her Back


The bell has rung, and of course this is when your girlfriend starts sending message after message. If you don't want her to get seriously mad, you'll have to hide your phone under the desk and text her back. Just don't let the teacher catch you.

Watch the Teacher


Look around the classroom. Use the teacher's footsteps and voice to figure out where they are. When they're far enough away, look down, type the prompted letters, and send your reply. When they get close, put the phone away immediately and look up like you've been paying attention the whole time.

Expect the Unexpected


Of course, it won't be that easy. A video might suddenly play out loud. A private message might go to the class group chat. You might even fart at the worst possible moment. Sometimes the lecture stops without warning, and the teacher appears somewhere they absolutely should not be.

Teachers may also walk over to check your desk and the cubby underneath. Quickly slide your phone into your sleeve before they inspect it, then try to look innocent.

Can you keep your girlfriend happy, look like the most attentive student in the room, and survive all four classes?

Four Classes to Survive


1. Four increasingly difficult classes
2. Strange phenomena
3. Embarrassing incidents
4. Normal and Extreme modes with lesson-specific time limits

The video shows only the first lesson. As you progress through the levels, the challenge gets much tougher, and even more unexpected events await. Take on the challenge!

Lead a small tribe from the Stone Age to a futuristic civilization in a card-based strategy game focused on resource management, production, and technological progress.

Gather resources, assign workers, build settlements, and discover new technologies as your civilization grows. Expand your economy, optimize production chains, and unlock entirely new ways to play with every technological era.

The full game will span seven unique eras of human development, introducing new mechanics, buildings, resources, and strategic possibilities along the way.

As your civilization expands, you'll encounter other settlements. Establish trade routes, send caravans, build diplomatic relations, or wage war to secure your future. Every decision shapes the path of your civilization.

Key Features

• Build and optimize a growing production system

• Manage workers and expand your settlement

• Progress through seven technological eras

• Unlock new technologies, buildings, and resources

• Trade, negotiate, or conquer neighboring civilizations

• Relaxing strategy with deep management systems

The demo includes the opening Stone Age era and introduces the core mechanics that drive the full game.

Your wallet is empty. Your family owes the bank $78,150. All you have is an old laptop and a very bad idea.

TEEN HUSTLER is a story-driven hacking and business sim. You play a broke 20-year-old in Shadow City who must pay off the debt before the bank takes the apartment. Work honest office shifts, run small businesses, mine crypto, take risky contracts on the dark web, and stay one step ahead of the police.

Five story chapters, four endings, about 2 hours of play: go legit, go dark, get busted, or run.

KEY FEATURES

• Living 3D room. Sleep, eat, pay the electricity bill (or sit in the dark), and move up from a run-down flat to a bunker or a high-tech penthouse.







• Retro OS desktop. Click through TapHustle, the CoinTrade exchange, the GigLink messenger, ShadowShop and the HEVIOS rig console.

• ShadowNet & darknet contracts. Break into systems with puzzle minigames, steal data, launder dirty money. Every dirty job raises your police heat, and if the cops come for you, you may end up behind bars.

• Build your own mining rig. Order the parts, assemble it, tune it in HEVIOS and keep it cool.


• Businesses and markets. Trade volatile coins on CoinTrade, buy ventures, hire managers, survive rivals and tax inspectors.

• Harbor smuggling. Assemble weapons at your workbench, pack the crate and get it past customs.

• Choices with consequences. Evening events, nosy neighbors, your mom, and a bank that does not wait.

• Retro arcade cabinet and a pixel slot machine for downtime (no real-money gambling).

Build an Economy. Master the Market. Outmanoeuvre Your Rivals.

Tempus Inceptum is a competitive economic strategy game set across procedurally generated hex worlds. Claim territory, exploit the resources the land provides, and turn raw materials into increasingly valuable goods through interconnected production chains.

But you are not building alone.

Rival AI factions develop their own economies alongside yours — claiming land, harvesting resources, producing goods and trading on the same dynamic market. Their decisions affect prices and opportunities, forcing you to adapt as the economy evolves.

Expand your territory. Specialise your production. Trade the market. Use tactical gambits against your competitors. There is no single route to economic dominance.

Your faction also builds a history of its own. The evolving Faction Journal records notable achievements, decisions and events from your games, creating a growing chronicle of the faction you have created.

And through shared daily, weekly and monthly challenges, you can put your strategy against other players facing the same economic conditions.

Build Around the World You Are Given

Every game begins on a procedurally generated hex landscape shaped by terrain, climate and available resources.

Choose where to establish yourself, claim new territory and build an economy around the opportunities the land provides. Farms, mines, lumber mills and other harvesting buildings supply the raw materials needed to support increasingly complex production networks.

A strong economy is not simply about building more. It is about building the right things, in the right places, at the right time.

Create Production Chains

Raw resources are only the beginning.

Transform them into more valuable products through interconnected production buildings. Crops can become food, ore can become steel, wood can become timber, and increasingly advanced goods can open new economic opportunities.

Your production network can grow in different directions depending on the resources available, the demands of the market and the strategy you choose to pursue.

Trade and Adapt

Resources and products can be bought and sold through the in-game Stock Exchange.

Prices move as supply and demand change during each game, creating opportunities for trade as well as production. Sell into strong markets, buy when prices are favourable, or use the exchange to support an economy that cannot produce everything it needs locally.

The strongest strategy may not always be the largest production network. Sometimes the better opportunity is simply recognising what the market is telling you.

Compete Against Rival Factions

AI factions operate under the same economic pressures as you.

They claim land, build harvesting and production networks, trade resources and pursue their own priorities. Their actions can alter the availability of territory, affect market prices and change which strategies remain attractive.

You are not solving an isolated optimisation puzzle. You are competing inside an economy that is changing around you.

Use Tactical Gambits

Economic competition does not have to remain peaceful.

Gambits give you ways to influence the contest beyond ordinary expansion and trade. Disrupt rival production, interfere with markets, protect your own faction or create temporary advantages when the opportunity arises.

Using them well means judging not only what benefits you, but when intervention is worth the cost.

Choose Your Route to Victory

Tempus Inceptum supports different approaches to economic success.

You might build broad production networks, specialise around a handful of valuable goods, expand aggressively across the map, exploit movements in the Stock Exchange or use gambits to undermine stronger rivals.

Different game modes place the emphasis on different measures of success, rewarding adaptation rather than a single fixed build order.

Take on Shared Challenges

Daily, weekly and monthly challenges give players the same underlying objective and economic conditions to compete against.

Rather than playing together in the same world, players tackle comparable scenarios independently and compete through shared leaderboards.

This makes each challenge a test of decision-making: given the same opportunity, what can you make of it?

Build a Faction History

The faction you create has an identity beyond a single result.

Your evolving Faction Journal records notable events, achievements and decisions from your games, gradually building a chronicle of what that faction has experienced.

It is a record of the strategies you tried, the successes you earned and the stories that emerged along the way.

Play at Your Own Pace

Alongside competitive challenges, sandbox and standard game modes let you experiment with production chains, markets and strategies without the same leaderboard pressure.

Learn the systems, try unusual approaches, refine your economic thinking — or simply build and see what happens.

Site 12. One pod, one core, and whatever you remember.

Terraform Co. runs the off-world division, and you just got posted to an unsurveyed plot on a green planet with nothing built on it. The company wants two things out of the rock, in this order: a working operation, and a profit.

You are #15 of 15 on the S&G-15, the planet's stock index. Fourteen companies are above you.

Factory feeds depot, depot feeds town, town pays for the next factory

That's the whole company, and it's the loop the entire game runs on.

Start with your hands. Clear dirt and rock with a pickaxe, tranq a native grazer and carry it back to a pen — grazers breed, and a full pen is a livelihood. Then stop doing it yourself. Belts haul while you're somewhere useful, automated miners work the ore you were chipping at, and machines turn all of it into things people will pay for.

  • Ore — crush, smelt and forge it into alloy, with sand, slag and glass falling out as byproducts you'll want to recycle rather than dump.
  • Premium metals — pulverize ingots to dust, enrich it with acid into pure alloy, and turn that into power cells.
  • Electronics — etch crystal dust into wafers and foil, assemble microchips, then smartphones, then laptops.
  • Food — the grazer line, all the way up to a suspiciously premium burger.
  • Chemicals — vats, acid, glycerin, dye and fragrance, gluing the organic and mineral sides together.
  • Five tech tiers, gated behind what you've actually produced — not a menu you buy your way through.

Then build the city that buys it

Product isn't money until somebody buys it, and nobody lives here yet. So you lay the first road.

Buy and place buildings, and the town grows on top of your factory's output. Residents move into your houses, drive and walk the streets you laid, and spend money in the shops you placed. But shops don't conjure stock — you supply them. Belt goods into a Cargo Depot and it runs vans out to every shop that wants them. New building types unlock from production milestones, so the town's growth is paced by the factory's.

It's a second economy stacked on the first, and it's alive down to street level: cars queue at junctions, pedestrians cross at the kerb, vans pull into loading bays.

Climb the S&G-15

Coins come from selling. Rank comes from contracts.

Each of the fourteen rival corporations has a fixed ladder of supply contracts in its sector. Clear a ladder and you overtake that company — a headline runs, and their trade secret becomes a permanent perk of yours. Ladder contracts are untimed, so they're the campaign; timed spot orders pay the bills in between.

A live headline engine moves sell prices with booms, bubbles and shortages, and rumours land about a day ahead of the effect — so a factory that's paying attention can build toward the spike. The market terminal puts the index board, contract ladders, spot orders, a price grid with sparklines and the news feed in one place.

Clear all fourteen ladders and Terraform Co. tops the index.

And the raiders

Alien raiders drop on the landing pad and run at your core — they want it shut down, and they'll help themselves to your stock on the way. It's an interruption to build against rather than the job itself.

Your bat never runs dry, which is the whole appeal of it. The tranq gun takes things alive. Raider types keep fixed identities from the first raid to the fortieth — runners are always faster than you, armored always shrug off the first few swings — so the pressure comes from numbers and composition, not from a stat slider quietly outpacing you.

Built to be looked at

Grounded industrial art direction: worn matte machinery, honest materials, real proportions, with saturated colour reserved strictly for the things you need to read at a glance. If it's glowing, it means something.

The build browser's icons are photographs of the actual buildings, taken by the game itself — so they can't go stale, and what you see in the menu is exactly what lands on the ground.

The planet is alive. And it does not want you here

You are a colonist. A teleporter has appeared in a strange new world, and all it can give you at the start is a single drone and a small reserve of resources.

Around you stretches an endless procedural world of mountains, lava lakes, mineral and thorium deposits, dense growth, and pockets of alien life.

For now, they do not know you are here.

Terrahold is a strategy sandbox about base building, economy, and defense on a living planet. There are no missions or hand-crafted levels. Every run takes place on a new procedural map, and you decide how fast and how far your colony expands.

Build and manage your colony

The teleporter is the heart of the colony. If it is destroyed, the run is over.

Robots construct and repair buildings, explore the map, and defend the base. They can make some decisions on their own, but from the strategic view you can still assign positions and targets directly. When you want to be in the fight or on the frontier yourself, switch to tactical control of a single defender or scout. That robot is under your full personal control, while the rest of the colony keeps working.

The colony depends on a shared power grid. Solar panels provide your first kilowatts, power lines connect distant outposts, and further expansion requires lava, thorium, thermal generators, and nuclear power plants.

Reshape the planet

Terrain is more than just an obstacle.

The Terraformer can tear down mountains and fill lava lakes, clearing space and creating new routes. Bridges can be built across narrow lava channels, shortening travel paths and allowing infrastructure to reach areas that were previously inaccessible.

Sometimes the best way around an obstacle is to change the map itself.

Defend what you build

Your main enemy is not a set of scripted waves, but the planet's ecosystem. Vines spread across the land and damage infrastructure. Spiders gather in groups and strike from the fog. Eggs hatch new creatures, while spore colonies make the surrounding vegetation even more dangerous.

The farther your colony spreads, the greater the pressure becomes.

Walls and turrets help hold the perimeter, while force field generators can cover critical parts of the base with a protective dome. The field absorbs damage instead of the buildings and units beneath it, draining energy from the grid until its reserve is exhausted.

Open the way home

Keeping the teleporter alive is not enough. To win, you must open a permanent tunnel into the network of worlds.

That requires a massive surplus of energy. Explore the map, secure thorium deposits, expand the grid, and bring nuclear power plants online.

Hold the colony. Build the power. Open the link.

Key Features

  • Endless procedural maps with varied terrain and resource distribution
  • Base building, resource extraction, and a shared power grid
  • Robots with partial autonomy and direct control when needed
  • Terraforming: remove mountains and fill lava lakes
  • Bridges across lava for new routes and infrastructure
  • Force fields that protect entire sections of the base by consuming grid energy
  • A reactive ecosystem instead of conventional scripted waves
  • Fog of war, exploration, and radar
  • Progression from solar power to thorium and nuclear energy
  • One objective: protect the teleporter and generate enough power to open a permanent tunnel

TOB is an oil tycoon game, where half the action takes place underground. You buy land plots, prospect for oil, and acquire infrastructure. You drill, pump the oil into barrels or storage tanks, and transport it using tankers or trucks. You can sell the oil to buyers or sign contracts for delivery at a set price. Play through a 200-day story campaign, then keep your oil business running for as long as you like. Profitability is dictated by the market - politics, weather and collusion. Many factors influence the prices of oil and real estate. Rounding out the experience is Tex - a well-known, cheerful character who introduces himself during the game's opening minutes.

Find it

Use sonar that scans the ground thoroughly, much like resonance imaging. The results will provide the estimated size of the deposit, its depth, and the probability of oil actually being present - you must then decide whether to risk the cost of a dry well. You will carry out the actual drilling using a rig. The drill bit is capable of turning and creating branches.

Build the network

Multiple pumps can extract oil from a single reservoir, while a single pump can draw oil from multiple reservoirs. This enables the optimization of oil recovery in terms of time and cost, allowing you to choose the specific type of optimization you need most at any given moment.

Play the market

The price of oil fluctuates based on random market events. You can - and initially, you even have to - sell to a local buyer immediately after extraction for a fraction of the price. Alternatively, you can read the papers, listen to Tex, store the oil and wait for favorable selling conditions. But, as is the nature of the market, the outcome can vary.

Move the oil

Trucks and tankers transport crude oil from storage tanks to warehouses, collection points, or contract customers. Refineries, railways, and the military pay a premium for timely delivery, especially under strict contract terms. Worn-out vehicles belch smoke and crawl back to the garage - they require constant maintenance.

Build a crew

Field operators take over your routine tasks: operating pumps and arranging the transport of oil to storage or to a buyer. Additionally, more skilled operators can handle transport from storage, sign contracts based on set terms, and ensure timely fleet maintenance. You can organize operators into teams and issue single commands to entire teams - a classic example of business scaling.

Expand across Texas

Ten fields available for purchase, each with its own land, deposits, and infrastructure. Variable, unpredictable weather. Mail arriving every few days, offering a glimpse into an uncertain future. Plenty of planning and forward thinking.

A story, then a sandbox

A 200-day story campaign (15-25 hours) with Tex, the mail and the market headlines. When it ends, your fields keep running: endless play with random events.

The whole description sounds serious, but there’s also a cow on the roof and beer with the operators. Good luck in Texas and have fun! :)

about_html:
ONE MOUNTAIN, ONE GOAL

That Mountain Needs to Fall is a short incremental game about dwarves, Norse mythology and mining.

Damage the rock to send ore flying, haul it to the Warehouse, sell, build and raise an army, call on the powers of the gods and receive Odin's blessings.

MINE, HAUL, SELL, UPGRADE

  • Break. Deal damage, knock ore loose.

  • Grab. Every chunk flies off the rock, lands in the collection area and piles up. Carriers pick it up and walk it to the Warehouse. If they fall behind, the pile just keeps growing.

  • Sell for gold and spend it on houses, new dwarves and upgrades. Or send the ore to the Forge and smelt it into material for better gear.

THE SKY WORKS TOO

Each mountain can bring an event: lightning striking the rock, a starfall, a hurricane that sucks up the ore, a snowball rolling down the slope, an eclipse that stores your damage and releases it in a flash. And sometimes Nidhogg flies overhead and sets everything on fire.

A VILLAGE FULL OF UPGRADES

Build a whole village at the foot of the mountain. Every building has its own shop, and many upgrades stay hidden until you earn them.

UNLEASH RAGNAROK, RETURN WITH ODIN'S BLESSINGS

Every mountain you bring down earns Odin points, but you can only spend them after the end of the world. When you're ready, unleash Ragnarok: you lose your gold, your dwarves and your village, and keep Odin's favor with game-changing upgrades.

Piece Together a Coherent Past from Fragmented Memories

Return to the aftermath of World War I, as the Austro-Hungarian Empire slowly falls apart. You play as the owner of a civilian trading post, running a strange little shop and reliving one three-day cycle after another through your memories. Survive a total of 30 days, reconstruct what really happened, and convince your family that everything you remember was real.

Escalating Difficulty and a Story-Rich Experience

The controls are intentionally simple: mouse clicks, SPACE to skip, and ESC to exit. Within the game, you can trade goods, predict prices, head out to purchase supplies, and even... banish demons and murder customers.

Manipulate prices, resell supplies for profit, monitor the condition of both your shop and yourself, and survive 30 full days under increasingly brutal conditions.

By sheer coincidence, you now control the entire town's supply routes. But how much money you can make from them is not really what matters to you.

The real reason you remain in this town is that the old aristocracy murdered your business partner in an attempt to seize his convoy. But now that control of the convoy has passed to you, their attention has turned to you as well...

Trade, Then Kill

There are many ways to die during a run, any one of which can bring the game to an end: starvation, freezing to death, loss of faith, being reported for murder... Just like countless others struggling to survive in 1918, the shopkeeper you play in these memories faces danger from every direction.

But you possess one enormous advantage: your convoy gives you the power to manipulate the prices of goods across the entire town. At the same time, an unexpected group of people approaches you. They will become important pieces in the plan you are building within the town, while the violence hidden inside you begins to spread.

Most of the time, you can simply trade and deal with the people of the town. Building relationships with them may help lead you toward a better ending. But you must still complete your objectives—otherwise, the story will come to an abrupt end.

Tarot Cards? Anomalies?

For reasons you cannot fully understand, your mind has fallen into confusion. Perhaps it is the drugs. Perhaps it is exhaustion.

Whatever the cause, strange anomalies begin appearing inside your memories: lights flicker, the stove suddenly goes out, your backpack disappears, prices printed in books become corrupted, newspapers turn completely blank...

You interpreted all of these events as omens foretold by the Tarot. And so, within your memories, Tarot cards can be used to aid you.

The Fool grants you one extra day.

The Sun grants you money that continues to stack over time.

The Tower wipes out all of your money, but doubles your goods.

Death leaves you on the brink of dying—but in return, it also allows you to kill a customer...

Find the anomalies, and obtain Tarot cards.

Keep Track of the Town's Resource Prices in Real Time

You possess an extraordinary talent for business. If you truly wanted to, you could even make leather more expensive than gold.

Use the trading panel to purchase supplies and keep track of the constantly changing prices of every resource. You are the Price Setter—the one who decides the price of every deal.

About the economic systems: The game intentionally simplifies the real-world mechanisms of price manipulation in order to create a more engaging gameplay experience.

Some cats know exactly what they want. It's your job to figure it out.

Load up on tasty meals and set out to feed the cats of the world. Every city has its own hungry regulars — and every one of them has opinions. Serve the right dish and hearts fly. Serve the wrong one and... well. That's not their bowl.

  • COOK — Chop, blend, and simmer real recipes step by step in your cozy kitchen. Nail the skill check for a perfect batch, and upgrade your tools until production purrs along on its own.

  • LEARN — Cats show you what they love (and refuse what they don't). Preparing meals to match the feeding location needs  is half of the success.

  • TRAVEL — Feed your way through cities around the globe, from lantern-lit streets at dusk to new horizons. Meet new cats and test their tongues.

  • COLLECT — Fill your collection with dozens of cat breeds and recipes, complete achievements, and unwind with the in-game jukebox.

A relaxed, huggable game about the world's most demanding food critics.

In 1938, an expedition was organized under the codename Last Breath, whose objective was to achieve the deepest manned immersion in history, explore and scan life from the abyssal depths, and extract using a mechanical arm a sample of an inexhaustible energy source discovered in the Earth’s core, with the potential to transform the fate of humanity.

No one wanted to take part in this dangerous mission… except John, a man devastated by guilt after an accident that destroyed his life. For him, this mission is not science: it is penance.

Aboard a tiny scientific mini‑submarine barely 3×2 meters in size, equipped with archaic systems typical of the 1930s, John must survive the most hostile journey ever attempted, while solving escape‑room‑style puzzles and facing extreme conditions and abyssal anomalies capable of distorting reality and the senses.

The descent to 10,000 feet leads him into a hell of pressure and heat comparable to that of a star. But the abyss will not be his only enemy: the anomalies begin to manipulate the memories of his lost family, confronting him with what torments him most and triggering his emotional disintegration.

The experience blends claustrophobia and constant tension with psychological horror, in which John must face not only the cold, hostile abyss, but also his own demons, in a descent that will ultimately lead him into his own personal abyss.

Spyke is a go-getter. He moved himself up the ranks at Zoid Corp. like no other Animoid before. But when he sees too much, he loses everything and has to find a way to make things right again. 

The Adventure of Spyke is a classically styled 3D top-down action RPG that takes place across a vast world. Explore forgotten puzzle-filled vaults, bustling cities, and beautiful landscapes. Battle robots, organ-harvesters, and terrifying creatures to not only save Spyke but uncover a deep mystery at the heart of reality itself.

Game Features

  • Classic top-down action RPG gameplay using just a game controller.

  • Deep story with extensive lore, characters, and story.

  • Puzzle-based item and inventory system. Place, rotate, and connect kanjicite crystals to make new items with new enchantments.

  • Find a vast array of melee weapons, projectile weapons, shields, and more.

  • Enchant weapons, projectiles, and shields with different elements you can switch between on the fly to test your wits and reflexes.

  • Further enchant weapons with different modifiers to add even more abilities, such as scanning to see enemies' strengths and weaknesses.

  • Connect crystals in a chain going from element, through modifiers, and then to an implement to create your own custom items.

  • Utilize a logical mana system that requires planning and balancing to achieve the right balance for your weapon set.

  • Explore cavernous vaults to find new items, enemies, paths, and more.

  • Create special kanjicite from their parts.

  • Collect all the kanjicite you can! A revolutionary system helps the user locate and use found kanjicite with just a game controller.

Not Just A Game

What a sport like soccer/football is to a gym workout, The Adventure of Spyke is to education.

  • Item system helps player learn to recognize Chinese and Japanese characters and learn new words.

  • Game dialogue uses challenging words but explains them in context.

  • Unique puzzles help player learn a variety of subjects, including STEM concepts from mathematics and engineering.

  • In game economy and currency system helps player understand banking and basic finance.

  • More to come that will inspire you to want to learn more -- no concepts are pushed upon the user, but rather the user is pulled into new concepts that can be immediately applied in-game in a practicum-style learning environment.

  • Puzzles and gameplay designed by MIT-educated electrophysics PhD scientist/programmer.

ABOUT THIS GAME

The Adventurer's Guild Idler is a fantasy idle adventure game where you manage a guild and watch your adventurers set out into a dangerous world.

Send parties of heroes beyond the guild, where they will encounter demons, monsters, powerful commanders and other dangers. Your adventurers fight automatically, gain experience and collect rewards as they push further into the world.

There are clicker mechanics where you click on your Guild Master desk to do some work and earn gold in return. Sell their loot, upgrade your guild, apply skills to your adventurers, and keep growing stronger to overcome the demon army.

STRENGTHEN YOUR PARTY

a party with different roles:

  • Tank — protects the party from danger.

  • Warrior — gets into the thick of combat.

  • Mage — brings powerful magical attacks.

  • Ranger — attacks enemies from a distance.

Watch your party work together as they travel through the world and fight their way through the demon army.

ADVENTURE, FALL, RETURN

Not every expedition goes according to plan.

Your adventurers can be defeated during their journey. When the entire party falls, they revive at the guild portal room and then go through a short training session before setting out again.

Each time they return, they will train in the training area until all members have gathered at the training spot. You can apply skill points using your Guild Training book. You can also improve their skills when they are on their expedition, letting you influence the outcome of their battles.

GROW YOUR ADVENTURERS

Your heroes gain experience as they adventure and develop over time. Use your adventurer's training book to upgrade their main attributes and make them stronger.

The further they travel, the stronger the enemies become. Improve your adventurers and see how far they can push into the world.

A GUILD THAT NEVER STOPS

When the party falls, the world resets to the most recent level that has not been completed yet.

Sell the loot they bring back, grow the guild's economy, upgrade the guild and improve your adventurers. Then watch the party prepare and set out again.

The goal is simple: keep improving the guild and your adventurers until they can overcome the demon army.

The guild awaits. The next adventure begins.

Restore the gallery. Then make the world your own.

You are the keeper of a gallery left in disarray. Explore its rooms, collect paintings, study the clues around you, and return each work to the wall where it belongs. Arrange complete exhibitions, adjust their lighting, and take on timed assignments that reward a careful eye—and a little speed.

Away from the gallery, every room becomes a space for personal expression. Buy furniture, decorations, tools, and strange little objects, then place, recolor, move, rotate, and resize them. Paint original canvases with a range of brushes and colors, save your work, and hang it in the world. Take photographs, display your favorite images, and choose the music that gives each room its atmosphere.

You can also sketch shapes in mid-air and turn your strokes into physical creations. Draw something rigid, add working wheel parts, and release the finished assembly into the world. Build a bridge, sketch a sword, or invent a rolling contraption—then give it a shove and discover whether it rolls, holds together, or collapses spectacularly.

Between gallery assignments, explore a collection of compact challenges involving spatial reasoning, routes, codes, rotating pipes, painting, and observation. Quiet creativity and timed puzzle pressure sit side by side, letting you decide whether to carefully curate or simply experiment.

Throughout it all, the paintings and rooms preserve fragments of someone else’s life. Nothing explains the whole story. Instead, meaning emerges through images, objects, sounds, and the spaces you restore.

Who lived this life before you—and what did they leave behind?

Features

  • Restore exhibitions by finding paintings, interpreting clues, and placing each work where it belongs.

  • Work with a collection of more than 400 paintings, culminating in a large 15-category sorting challenge.

  • Paint original canvases and display your creations in the world.

  • Sketch in 3D and transform freehand strokes into rigid or wheeled physics objects.

  • Buy, place, recolor, rotate, resize, and arrange furniture and unusual objects.

  • Experiment with physics and see whether your creations roll, balance, collide, or fall apart.

  • Shape the atmosphere with lighting, music, images, and your own photographs.

  • Play a variety of bite-sized creative, spatial, and logic challenges.

  • Uncover a quiet mystery told through paintings, rooms, and the traces of a life left behind.

The board

The Attending is a management sim about one night shift in an emergency department. You don't build anything. You run the board. You put patients in beds, give cases to your doctors, and sign the plans that send people home or upstairs.

Your doctors

You work with six doctors, and each one has their own speed, habits and blind spots. Some sign fast and sound sure. Some take longer and tell you when they aren't sure. When one of them brings you a discharge, the chart shows what they did and what they skipped. If you sign the wrong one, the debrief shows the minute you signed it.

Stepping in

You can take a case over or order a test yourself. If you were right, that doctor trusts you more. If you were wrong, you lose some of their trust, and you will need it later when the board is full and someone is at the lockers with their coat on.

The rest of the night

Two patients come in drunk after a fall, and one of them is bleeding inside his skull. A family at the desk knows something the triage note missed. A doctor closes the curtain and tells you about a dose they doubled. Your doctors have their own problems tonight too, like a father in a bed upstairs or a son at home with a fever.

  • Each patient's diagnosis is set before the shift starts. The serious cases get worse over time, and you can pause whenever you want.
  • Signing off is the core skill. You read the workup, decide what still needs checking, and live with the result.
  • Some cases come in pairs. A kidney stone and a torn aorta arrive with the same complaint, and only the workup tells them apart.
  • The debrief rebuilds every miss to the minute. It shows when the finding went on the chart and when the discharge was signed.
  • Admitted patients wait in their ER bed until a bed opens upstairs. You can call the bed manager to move one along, and the call costs you minutes.
  • 28 dilemmas, each written for a moment in the shift, like an argument at the desk, a doctor walking out, or a family that wants a transfer to another hospital. Each one costs time, trust or both.
  • Up to three featured patients a night. Some bring a family member, and the debrief tells you how each one ended.
  • 28 kinds of patient, from a toothache to a ruptured ectopic pregnancy.
  • Each night is generated and plays in one sitting.

Character portraits by John Dervishi. Hospital artwork, key art and logo by Angela Maldonado Jaime.
